However, existing stealthy projector-based adversarial attack methods model the project-and-capture process in a single and static view, limiting their view-invariant capability and practical applicability in dynamic environments. In this paper, we introduce View-Invariant Projector-Based Adversarial Attack (VIPA), a novel method designed to overcome these limitations by achieving both view-invariant and classifier-agnostic adversarial attacks in the physical world. We first leverage a view-invariant projector-camera system simulation method to model the physical interactions between projected patterns and real-world surfaces. To ensure robustness and stealthiness of the attack across different views, VIPA optimizes adversarial projections by aggregating simulated attack losses from multiple views. This joint optimization across diverse views helps maintain robustness regardless of the viewpoints. Finally, the optimized patterns are physically projected into real-world scenes, where they successfully fool various classifiers from different viewpoints, thereby enabling robust and practical view-invariant adversarial attacks. Our experiments in both targeted and untargeted attacks demonstrate that VIPA consistently achieves higher attack success rates than existing methods, while also enhancing stealthiness and ensuring minimal perceptual degradation across all tested views.

llm.title_ja: VIPA：視点不変プロジェクタベース敵対的攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: 画像分類器を誤動作させるプロジェクタベースの敵対的攻撃において、動的な環境や様々な視点に対応するため、複数視点からのシミュレーション損失を統合して最適化する「VIPA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のプロジェクタベースの敵対的攻撃は単一の静的視点における投影を前提としており、視点不変性や動的環境への適用性が限られている。
llm.method: 視点不変のプロジェクタ・カメラシステムシミュレーションを用いて物理的相互作用をモデル化し、複数の視点からシミュレートされた攻撃損失を集約して敵対的投影を最適化する。
llm.result: 実世界における実験において、テストされたすべての視点において知覚的な劣化を最小限に抑えつつ、従来手法よりも高い攻撃成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: コンピュータビジョン

2611.07441.title: Closed-Loop Physics-Based Manipulation Evaluation at a Commodity Price: What 4.4 L4 GPU hours at $3.50 Buys You
2611.07441.abstract: Running evaluations of contact-rich robotic manipulation at statistical scale has largely been possible only at well-resourced labs, highlighting the need for affordable and efficient options for broader audiences. We present a reproducible evaluation harness wrapper based on a previous study at 200-rollout scale on serverless commodity GPUs, at a cost of approximately $3.50 USD and 38 minutes of wall-clock per replication (4.4 L4-GPU-hours across eight parallel shards). Using the harness, we report a partially controlled negative result on action chunking with sparse data: three independently trained chunked checkpoints produce zero genuine successes across 780 rollouts, while three single-step checkpoints range from 2.6% to 11.8% success rate. A per-step-replanning control partially isolates chunk prediction, rather than open-loop chunk execution as the mechanism, with the failure localized to the training formulation and multi-step prediction. This work further democratizes physics-based policy development and evaluation through our reusable harness.
2611.07441.comment: 4 pages, 2 figures. Accepted to IROS 2026 Workshop on Building Scalable Infrastructure for Robot Learning: From Data Scaling to Real-World Deployment

llm.title_ja: 手頃な価格での閉ループ物理ベースマニピュレーション評価：4.4時間のL4 GPUと3.50ドルで得られるもの
llm.tldr_ja: 接触リッチなロボットマニピュレーションの統計的規模での評価を低コストで行うための再現可能な評価ハーネスを提案し、スパースデータを用いたアクションチャンキングに関する否定的な結果を報告する。
llm.problem: 接触リッチなロボットマニピュレーションの統計的規模での評価は十分に予算のある研究室でしか行えず、より広範なアクセスのための手頃なオプションが不足している。
llm.method: サーバーレスの安価なGPUを用いて、200ロールアウト規模、コスト約3.50ドル、約38分で実行可能な再現性の高い評価ハーネスラッパーを構築する。
llm.result: アクションチャンキングを用いたチェックポイントが780回のロールアウトで成功率ゼロとなった一方、単一ステップのチェックポイントは2.6%〜11.8%の成功率を記録した。

2611.07437.title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing
2611.07437.abstract: We present IMUDINO, the first foundation model (FM) for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse sensing tasks including human activity recognition (HAR), health, motion capture, and odometry. Prior inertial FMs often focus on one subfield of inertial sensing and sometimes underperform state-of-the-art supervised methods (e.g., in HAR), making their scope considerably narrower than FMs for vision and natural language. Moreover, they often require fixed input length and sampling rate, and generalize poorly to unseen sensor locations. To build a general-purpose foundation model for inertial sensing, we adapt the DINO self-supervised learning (SSL) paradigm to inertial data through a set of semantics-preserving motion transformations that simulate variations in motion pattern and sensor setup. For model architecture, we use a plain transformer encoder with frequency-aware positional encoding that natively supports varying input length and sampling rate. This simple setup proved remarkably effective for learning global and dense features generalizable across users, sensor setups, tasks, and, in the case of robot odometry, embodiments. We hope IMUDINO can serve as a backbone for inertial sensing and kickstart the development of general-purpose inertial FMs.

llm.title_ja: IMUDINO：慣性センシングのための自己蒸留型基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 行動認識やモーションキャプチャ、オドメトリなど多様な慣性センシングタスクで優れた性能を達成する、慣性センシング向け初の基盤モデル「IMUDINO」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来の慣性センシング向け基盤モデルは特定のサブフィールドに偏っており、入力長やサンプリングレートが固定され、未見のセンサー配置への汎化性能が低い。
llm.method: DINO自己教師あり学習パラダイムを慣性データに適応させ、多様なモーションパターンやセンサー設定を模倣する意味保存型モーション変換を用いる。アーキテクチャには可変長・可変サンプリングレートをサポートする周波数認識型位置エンコーディング付きのTransformerエンコーダを採用する。
llm.result: 多様なユーザ、センサー設定、タスク、さらにはロボットオドメトリの形態にわたって汎化するグローバル・密な特徴量を学習できることを示した。
keywords_ja: モーションキャプチャ

2611.07417.title: MessyNav: Zero-Shot Navigation via Manipulation in Messy Environments
2611.07417.abstract: Real-world environments are messy, with paths often blocked by everyday objects like chairs and toys, requiring robots to perform interactive navigation by manipulating obstacles to clear a path. Existing methods rely on extensive simulation-based learning or per-scene instructions specifying which objects to avoid or manipulate. They struggle to generalize across novel objects, diverse environments, and varied contexts such as a cart of fragile glassware that should be avoided while an empty one can be pushed. We formalize this problem as open-world interactive navigation and present MessyNav, a zero-shot framework based on vision-language models (VLMs). At its core, MessyNav performs explicit VLM-based affordance reasoning before task planning to decide whether to swipe, pick up, or avoid an object and produce a high-level plan. Evaluated on a mobile manipulator across real-world indoor and outdoor environments, MessyNav improves success rate by 27 percentage points (pp) over the strongest baseline in real-robot trials and achieves statistically significant gains in a larger-scale offline evaluation, without task-specific training.

llm.title_ja: MessyNav: 散らかった環境におけるマニプレーションを介したゼロショットナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 未知の物体や環境に対応するため、ビジョン言語モデルを用いたアフォーダンス推論とタスク計画を統合し、タスク特化型の訓練なしでオープンワールドのインタラクティブナビゲーションを実現するフレームワークMessyNavを提案した。
llm.problem: 日常的な物体に経路を塞がれた散らかった環境で、ロボットが未知の物体に対して一般化して対話型ナビゲーションを行うこと。
llm.method: タスク計画の前に明示的なVLMベースのアフォーダンス推論を行い、移動、把持、回避のいずれを行うかを決定する。
llm.result: 実世界での試行において最強のベースラインと比較して成功率を27ポイント向上させ、大規模なオフライン評価でも統計的に有意な改善を達成した。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーター

2611.07411.title: Kinematic Hypothesis Context: Embodiment-Conditioned Learned Video Coding for Bandwidth-Limited Robot Policy Uplinks
2611.07411.abstract: Robots increasingly run large vision-language-action policies on remote servers, making the camera uplink the bottleneck. Existing video codecs spend bits on content the receiver could predict: the robot's own motion. We introduce the kinematic hypothesis context, a zero-rate conditioning signal that both ends build from joint states, the robot model and the camera calibration. Ego-motion homographies, per-link robot reprojections, an end-effector plane and a background memory warp the previous reconstruction into hypotheses that condition a learned video codec. We prove that history-only and global-pose conditioning with a limited receptive field cannot access this information under large motion, and that coding gains become task gains at the policy's success cliff. On LIBERO, the context saves 23.9% bit rate over a capacity-matched history-conditioned codec and 40-56% over x264, x265 and SVT-AV1, and needs 23.2% fewer bits than DCVC-RT at equal policy action deviation; trained to lower rates, it matches DCVC-RT in PSNR. In closed loop at equal rate, OpenVLA-OFT success nearly doubles from 22.8% to 43.1% at 6 kbps (72.6% with lower-rate training, 23.6 points above DCVC-RT), pi_0.5 success rises from 55.5% to 77.4%, and the gain grows under packet loss. The context transfers across three codec hosts and to real robot data.
2611.07411.comment: 15 pages, 12 figures. Preprint; supplementary material and code to be released upon formal publication

llm.title_ja: 運動学的仮説コンテキスト：帯域制限されたロボット方策アップリンクのための身体性条件付き学習型ビデオ符号化
llm.tldr_ja: 関節状態やカメラ較正等から得られるゼロレートの条件付け信号である運動学的仮説コンテキストを導入し、帯域制限された環境下でのリモートロボット方策の追従性能を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: リモートサーバー上で大規模なVLA方策を実行する際、カメラのアップリンクが帯域のボトルネックとなること。
llm.method: 関節状態、ロボットモデル、カメラ較正を用いて両端で構築するゼロレートの条件付け信号「運動学的仮説コンテキスト」を学習型ビデオコーデックに組み込む。
llm.result: LIBERO環境においてビットレートを23.9%〜56%削減し、OpenVLA-OFTやpi_0.5などの閉ループ制御における成功率を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: 運動学的コンテキスト

2611.07403.title: Dynamic Watermarking and Action-Conditioned Latent Dynamics for Secure Vision-Based Controllers
2611.07403.abstract: Replay attacks are difficult to detect in vision-based control systems because previously recorded observations can remain plausible while the physical system follows a different trajectory. This paper develops an adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework for detecting replay attacks against vision-based controllers. A private Gaussian watermark is added to the nominal control input, and a control input-conditioned latent dynamics network (LDN) predicts the corresponding evolution in a compact latent space learned from image observations. Attack evidence is obtained from the discrepancy between the predicted latent response and the latent representation of the received image observation. A reinforcement learning policy adjusts the watermark covariance using the latent state and detector confidence, thereby balancing attack detectability, watermark energy, and control distortion. A Lagrangian penalty on task-specific safety costs is included during training to limit the adverse effect of the excitation. The framework is evaluated on a vision-guided UR5 manipulation task in which the robot reaches a target while avoiding a moving human arm under nominal and replay-attacked observations.
2611.07403.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, Submitted to ACC 2027 conference

llm.title_ja: セキュアな視覚ベース制御のための動的ウォーターマーキングと行動条件付き潜在ダイナミクス
llm.tldr_ja: ビジョンベース制御システムにおけるリプレイ攻撃を検出するため、プライベートなガウスウォーターマークと行動条件付き潜在ダイナミクスネットワークを組み合わせた適応型動的ウォーターマーキングフレームワークを開発した。
llm.problem: ビジョンベース制御システムにおいて、過去に記録された観測データがもっともらしさを保つためリプレイ攻撃の検出が困難であること。
llm.method: 制御入力にプライベートなガウスウォーターマークを追加し、行動条件付き潜在ダイナミクスネットワークにより画像観測から予測される潜在表現の不一致から攻撃の証拠を得る。
llm.result: 動く人間の腕を避けながらターゲットに到達するビジョン誘導型UR5マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、攻撃の検出性、ウォーターマークのエネルギー、制御の歪みのバランスを取りながら有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: 動的ウォーターマーキング

2611.07378.title: Adversarial Multiplicity: Cherry-Picked Models and the Limits of Disclosure
2611.07378.abstract: Predictive multiplicity -- where similarly accurate models disagree on individual predictions -- can be leveraged to optimize secondary metrics (e.g., fairness) without loss in predictive performance. However, exploiting multiplicity opens the opportunity for motivated parties (or coding agents gaming their objectives) to steer predictions toward their own ends, such as in litigation or consumer disputes with automated decision-making tools. In these adversarial multiplicity settings, we distinguish soft manipulation, where parties optimize over innocuous model choices (e.g., hyperparameter tuning, feature engineering), from hard manipulation, where parties directly perturb model parameters. We find a sufficiently flexible model can be manipulated to reverse any individual prediction with minimal change in predictive performance while passing black-box audits, making hard manipulation viable in most regulatory settings. Soft manipulation has smaller effects but can pass white-box audits requiring full access to code and data. Even aggregate estimates can be manipulated: a model's estimated effect of climate change on wildfires can be fully reversed by hard edits and soft search. We find the Reconcile algorithm typically resolves most disagreements between models, but more often in favor of the manipulator when the opposing model is chosen adversarially compared to at random. We map which manipulations can plausibly pass existing regulations and disclosure policies, and recommend mitigations such as pre-registration, proof of model training, sensitivity analyses, multi-metric evaluations, and committing to versioned public models.

llm.title_ja: 敵対的多様性：チェリーピックされたモデルと開示の限界
llm.tldr_ja: 予測的多様性を悪用してモデルの予測を意図的に操作する「敵対的多様性」の問題を分析し、既存の規制や開示方針の下ですり抜けうる操作の範囲をマッピングして対策を提案した。
llm.problem: 同様に正確なモデルが個別の予測で意見が分かれる予測的多様性が、訴訟や消費者紛争などで意図的な操作に悪用される可能性があること。
llm.method: ハイパーパラメータ調整等のソフト操作と、モデルパラメータを直接摂動させるハード操作に分けて分析し、ブラックボックスおよびホワイトボックス監査での影響を検証する。
llm.result: 十分な柔軟性を持つモデルは、ブラックボックス監査を通過しながら最小限の性能低下で任意の個別予測を反転させることが可能であることを示した。

2611.07293.title: An Ordering Optimization for Fruit-Vegetable in High-Density Environment based on Genetic Algorithm
2611.07293.abstract: This paper presents a robotic harvesting method that combines RGB-D fruit localization, GA-based harvest ordering, and waypoint-based robot motion in dense and unstructured crop environments. The global RGB-D camera provides 3D fruit positions for ordering, while the end-effector-mounted camera provides close-range observation during execution. The GA determines the harvesting sequence, and static or dynamic waypoints define the intermediate robot motion. The method was evaluated in a controlled laboratory testbed and in four-, five-, and six-fruit field conditions. GA solutions were compared with exhaustive enumeration, and both waypoint offsets were examined by parameter sensitivity analysis. Continuous execution reduced unnecessary Home-return motion, while the dynamic waypoint changed with the remaining fruit distribution without changing the GA sequence. In the field evaluation, the dynamic-waypoint continuous strategy produced 40 collision events and a 70.7% target-approach success rate, compared with 55 collision events and 65.3% for the static-waypoint continuous strategy.

llm.title_ja: 遺伝的アルゴリズムに基づく高密度環境における果実・野菜の順序最適化
llm.tldr_ja: RGB-D果実局所化、遺伝的アルゴリズムによる収穫順序決定、ウェイポイントベースのロボット動作を組み合わせた高密度環境向けのロボット収穫手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 高密度で非構造化された作物環境において、効率的かつ衝突のないロボットによる果実収穫を行うこと。
llm.method: 大域的RGB-Dカメラで3D位置を取得し、遺伝的アルゴリズムで収穫順序を決定、エンドエフェクタ搭載カメラで近距離観測を行いつつウェイポイントで動作を定義する。
llm.result: 動的ウェイポイント連続戦略を用いたフィールド評価において、衝突回数を40回、ターゲット接近成功率70.7%を達成し、静的戦略よりも優れた性能を示した。

2611.07275.title: Efficient Diffusion Policy Fine Tuning with Latent Noise Representation Bridging
2611.07275.abstract: Pre-trained diffusion and flow policies have emerged as powerful backbones for robotics, yet adapting them to novel data via reinforcement learning (RL) remains computationally expensive, sample inefficient and lacks theoretical guarantees. Prior approaches that fine-tune the initial noise bypass costly backpropagation through time but struggle with the "noise aliasing" problem: there does not exista natural link between the noise space value and the action space value. This paper resolves these challenges by introducing the Latent Noise Linear Markov Decision Process (LNL-MDP). We derive the Bridge Equation for LNL-MDPs which eliminates the noise aliasing problem by aligning values with a shared representation between the noise and the action space. Furthermore, our LNL-MDP fine tuning framework falls under the FineTuneRL theory with near-optimal guarantee. Leveraging these insights, we propose Latent Representation Bridging for Diffusion (LARBRID), an algorithm that efficiently learns the representation to optimize the initial distribution that steers the pre-trained model to act optimally in the environment. It yields up to 2-3$\times$ performance increases on challenging control problems across a diverse suite of robotic locomotion and manipulation tasks. Code can be found at: github.com/Maincode-Research/LARBRID.git.
2611.07275.comment: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2026

llm.title_ja: 潜在ノイズ表現の橋渡しによる効率的な拡散ポリシーファインチューニング
llm.tldr_ja: 初期ノイズ空間と行動空間の間の値の不整合（ノイズエイリアシング）を解消するLatent Noise Linear MDP（LNL-MDP）を導入し、拡散ポリシーの強化学習による効率的なファインチューニングを実現した。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みの拡散ポリシーやフローポリシーを強化学習で新しいデータに適応させる際、計算コストが高くサンプル効率が悪く理論的保証が欠如していること。
llm.method: ノイズ空間と行動空間の間で表現を整列させるブリッジ方程式を導出し、環境内で最適に行動するように初期分布を最適化する表現学習アルゴリズム（LARBRID）を提案する。
llm.result: 多様なロボットの移動およびマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、困難な制御問題で2〜3倍の性能向上を実現した。
keywords_ja: ファインチューニング

2611.07272.title: VREgo: Consumer VR Headsets for Learning Robot Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations
2611.07272.abstract: VREgo trains manipulation policies from demonstrations recorded on consumer VR headsets; we instantiate it with EgoKit on one such headset, the PICO 4 Ultra. On-device head and hand tracking and stereo object localisation allow the operator to begin a demonstration at the table. We adapt HumanEgo's preprocessing to estimate grasp thresholds per recording, update object positions after release, and propagate segmentation masks between keyframes. We evaluate policies in simulation on two tabletop tasks recorded by one operator. For cube placement, we compare PICO and Project Aria recordings of the same 41 layouts. With 40 training demonstrations, the PICO policies placed the cube on the tray in 67, 74, and 60 of 100 evaluation layouts across three training seeds. The corresponding Aria results were 73, 78, and 0. For a two-stage stacking task recorded with the PICO alone, the baseline placed the block on the tray in 94 of 100 layouts and met the end-of-episode criterion for both placements in two. In one diagnostic episode, repeated replanning deferred release beyond the eight executed steps. Demonstration replays also showed that the open gripper could displace the cube before grasping it. After adapting the training trajectories and adding task-specific execution rules that use simulator object positions, the system met both placement criteria in 93.8% of episodes across four evaluation noise seeds. The same 100 layouts informed rule development and evaluation. VREgo is available at https://vrego.chuange.org/.

llm.title_ja: VREgo：一人称視点デモからロボットマニピュレーションを学習するための一般消費者向けVRヘッドセット
llm.tldr_ja: 一般消費者向けのVRヘッドセットを用いて記録された一人称視点のデモンストレーションからマニピュレーション方策を効率的に訓練するVREgoを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーションの方策を学習するために、特殊な装置を用いたデモンストレーション収集の手間がかかること。
llm.method: PICO 4 Ultraなどのコンシューマ向けVRヘッドセットのオンデバイス追跡とステレオ物体局所化を利用し、把持閾値の推定やセグメンテーションマスクの伝播を行う前処理を適用する。
llm.result: シミュレーション上の複数のタスクおよびレイアウトにおいて、限られたデモンストレーションから高い成功率でタスクを達成できることを示した。
llm.limitation: シミュレーション環境での評価が中心であり、実機での網羅的な検証にはタスク特化のルール調整等が必要であった

2611.07268.title: CRISP: Constraint-Resolved Interactions between Subsystems for Predictive Whole-Body Cooperation
2611.07268.abstract: This paper presents a layered control framework that recasts high-dimensional system dynamics as a composition of dynamically interconnected subsystems, with dynamic dual-arm manipulation on the humanoid serving as a representative application. The humanoid is decomposed into a single rigid body (SRB) representing the torso and floating-base dynamic models representing the articulated arms and lower-body. The rigid connections between arm and torso and the closed kinematic chain formed between the end-effectors during cooperative manipulation are represented as holonomic constraints. The corresponding Lagrange multipliers parametrize the interaction wrenches transmitted at the shoulders and between the end-effectors. The high-level nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) jointly optimizes the subsystem state trajectories, arm torques, ground reaction forces (GRFs), and interaction wrenches, enabling online wrench design and optimization while preserving the dynamic coupling among the independently modeled subsystems. The optimized arm torques are applied directly for cooperative dual-arm manipulation, whereas the prescribed GRFs are mapped to lower-body joint torque for whole-body coordination. We validate the proposed framework through numerical simulations and hardware experiments on a G1 humanoid robot. The results demonstrate optimal interaction wrenches consistent with simulated contact measurement, cooperative dual-arm trajectory tracking, and stable whole-body coordination while executing the NMPC in online manner.

llm.title_ja: CRISP：予測的全身協調のためのサブシステム間の制約解決型インタラクション
llm.tldr_ja: 高次元のシステムダイナミクスを動的に相互接続されたサブシステムの構成として再定義し、ヒューマノイドの協調両腕マニピュレーションにおいてオンラインでのレンチ設計と最適化を実現する階層型制御フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットによる動的な協調両腕マニピュレーションにおいて、全身の動的結合を維持しながら効率的な制御を行うこと。
llm.method: 胴体を表す単一剛体と、腕や下半身のモデルをホロノミック制約で接続し、ラグランジュ乗数で相互作用レンチをパラメトライズした上で、高レベルNMPCで統合最適化する。
llm.result: G1ヒューマノイドを用いた数値シミュレーションおよび実機実験により、シミュレーションされた接触測定と一致する最適な相互作用レンチと安定した全身協調を実証した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
両腕マニピュレーション

2611.07261.title: An Empirical Study of Reinforcement Learning for Keypoint Positioning of Deformable Linear Objects
2611.07261.abstract: Deformable linear object (DLO) manipulation is challenging because high-dimensional configurations, nonlinear contact dynamics, and diverse material and geometric properties produce a broad range of object responses that are both difficult to model and data-intensive to learn. This work studies reinforcement learning for planar manipulation of a one-end-grasped DLO, focusing on training efficiency, observation design, robustness, and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. We compare three Proximal Policy Optimization training stacks and find that the GPU-parallel MuJoCo Playground stack enables faster convergence and more consistent performance than CPU-based alternatives under the same wall-clock budget. Relative keypoint observations and an asymmetric actor-critic formulation further improve learning efficiency. Policies trained with observation noise, delay, domain randomization, and disturbances achieve simulation success rates of 96.4% for single-point tracking, 98.0% for disturbance recovery, and 88.8% for two-point tracking. Using markerless RGB-D keypoint estimation, the policies transfer without real-world fine-tuning, succeeding in 9/10, 10/10, and 8/10 physical trials, respectively.

llm.title_ja: 変形可能な線状物体のキーポイント位置決めにおける強化学習の実証的研究
llm.tldr_ja: 片端を把持された変形可能な線状物体（DLO）の平面マニピュレーションを対象に、GPU並列シミュレータを用いた強化学習による訓練効率やゼロショットSim-to-Real移行を実証的に研究した。
llm.problem: 変形可能な線状物体（DLO）は高次元の構成や非線形接触ダイナミクスを持つため、モデル化や学習が極めて困難であること。
llm.method: GPU並列のMuJoCo Playgroundスタックを活用したPPOによる訓練を行い、相対キーポイント観測と非対称アクター・クリティック定式化を比較評価する。
llm.result: シミュレーションで高い成功率を達成し、マーカーレスRGB-Dキーポイント推定を用いることで実機へのファインチューニングなしのゼロショット移行に成功した。

2611.07235.title: Adaptive Hybrid Force-Vision Control with EMG-Derived References for Deformable Bottle Manipulation
2611.07235.abstract: Robotic automation of laboratory tasks has become a growing interest to remove researchers from hazardous environments and repetitive procedures. However, even equipment as simple as squeeze bottles poses a challenging manipulation problem due to its deformability. This paper presents an adaptive hybrid vision-force controller for robotic grippers to effectively manipulate laboratory squeeze bottles to dispense liquid. This approach integrates force and vision feedback according to the interaction state, enabling effective squeezing while accounting for bottle deformation and recovery. The proposed controller is validated by comparing its performance with a pure force controller on 12 combinations of conditions consisting of 2 target dispense volumes, 2 plastic squeeze bottles, and 1 to 3 squeezes used to dispense. Human demonstrations of these operating conditions were collected using electromyography (EMG) sensing mapped to a desired grip force, which was then used as the force reference for the controllers to squeeze the bottles. Results demonstrated that the proposed adaptive hybrid vision-force controller achieved more accurate liquid dispensing with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 6.54 mL compared to a MAE of 15.92 mL from the pure force controller, while also replicating the human action recorded from the EMG signal more closely.

llm.title_ja: EMG由来の参照値を用いた変形可能なボトル操作のための適応型ハイブリッド力・視覚制御
llm.tldr_ja: インタラクション状態に応じて力と視覚のフィードバックを統合し、ボトルの変形と復元を考慮しながら実験室用スクイズボトルから正確に液体を吐出する適応型ハイブリッド制御手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 実験室の自動化において、スクイズボトルなどの変形しやすい容器の操作は、その変形特性のため困難なマニピュレーション課題であること。
llm.method: 筋電図（EMG）センサーから収集した人間のデモンストレーションを把持力にマッピングし、それを力参照値として用いる適応型ハイブリッド力・視覚コントローラーを構築する。
llm.result: 純粋な力コントローラーと比較して平均絶対誤差（MAE）を大幅に削減し（6.54 mL vs 15.92 mL）、人間の動作により近い液体吐出を実現した。

2611.07229.title: Spatial-UMI-Dream: Scaling World Action Models with Metric Geometry for UMI Manipulation
2611.07229.abstract: The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) enables scalable demonstration collection independently of a specific robot. However, its moving, close-range gripper cameras entangle camera and object motion without a stable external view, leaving the metric geometry needed for precise manipulation implicit in RGB. We introduce Spatial-UMI-Dream, a 5B spatial World Action Model (WAM) pretrained on 605 hours of RGB-D UMI data through two-stage training -- world-only adaptation followed by joint world-action learning -- to jointly predict future RGB, fisheye-aligned metric depth, and actions. Stereo-derived depth makes scene scale and spatial relationships explicit within a unified dual-gripper RGB-D representation. Furthermore, evaluating UMI policies requires testing whether UMI's robot-independent demonstration collection translates into policy generalization across robot embodiments, alongside robustness to environmental changes. We introduce RoboTwin-UMI, a twenty-task simulation benchmark built on RoboTwin with UMI wrist-mounted fisheye observations, enabling controlled, repeatable evaluation of UMI policies under environment and embodiment changes separately and jointly without additional fine-tuning. On RoboTwin-UMI, Spatial-UMI-Dream achieves 79.10% in-domain success and 72.15% under combined embodiment and environment shifts, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline in each setting by 4.65 and 10.30 percentage points, respectively. It also exhibits the smallest success-rate drop under embodiment transfer among the evaluated policies. In a matched pretraining ablation, RGB-only pretraining leads to a 5.75-percentage-point decrease in in-domain success compared with RGB-D pretraining. Across six real-world tasks, Spatial-UMI-Dream achieves 85.0% average success, exceeding the strongest baseline by 24.2 percentage points. Project page: https://weiduoyuan.com/spatial-umi-dream/

llm.title_ja: Spatial-UMI-Dream：メトリック幾何学を用いたUMIマニピュレーションのための世界行動モデルのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 605時間のRGB-D UMIデータで事前学習された50億パラメータの空間世界行動モデル「Spatial-UMI-Dream」を提案し、ロボット非依存のデモンストレーション収集と環境・身体性変化に対する優れた方策一般化を実現した。
llm.problem: UMIの移動式近接グリッパーカメラはカメラと物体の動きが絡み合い、正確なマニピュレーションに必要なメトリック幾何学が暗黙的になってしまうこと。
llm.method: ワールドのみの適応と共同ワールド・行動学習の2段階トレーニングを通じて、将来のRGB、魚眼整列メトリック深度、行動を共同予測する5Bの空間世界行動モデルを構築する。
llm.result: RoboTwin-UMIベンチマークにおいて、ドメイン内および身体性と環境の複合変化の双方でベースラインを大きく上回る成功率を達成し、6つの実世界タスクでも平均85.0%の成功率を記録した。
keywords_ja: ユニバーサルマニピュレーション

2611.07163.title: Distributed Geometric Optimization and Control of Rigid Differential-Drive Formations from Relative-Position Measurements
2611.07163.abstract: Distance based formation control fixes the shape of a robot team but leaves its position and orientation unconstrained. We regulate all three for differential drive robots that have only one absolute position anchor, absolute headings, body frame relative position measurements, and communication with their neighbors. We derive a two layer estimation control scheme directly from optimization. The first half of the result is a set of graph-proximal estimators that reconstruct the centroid, the anchor vector, and the centered coordinates. Exact proximal updates reach consensus in finitely many steps, and a finite number of primal dual iterations leaves a bounded reconstruction error. The controller combines proximal centroid and orientation steps with distance gradient shape regulation, and a finite rotation removes the orientation drift caused by the shape step. A discrete Lyapunov analysis gives local exponential convergence once the estimators have converged. We validate the method in ROS 2 Gazebo and in experiments with five physical robots.

llm.title_ja: 相対位置測定に基づく剛体差動駆動隊形の分散幾何学的最適化と制御
llm.tldr_ja: 絶対位置アンカーや車体フレーム相対位置測定を用いて、差動駆動ロボットチームの位置、向き、形状を同時に制御する2層の推定制御スキームを導出した。
llm.problem: 距離ベースのフォーメーション制御ではロボットチームの形状は固定されるものの、その位置や向きが制約されないこと。
llm.method: 重心、アンカーベクトル、中心座標を再構築するグラフ近傍推定器のセットと、近傍の重心・向きのステップと距離勾配形状規制を組み合わせたコントローラーを構築する。
llm.result: ROS 2 Gazeboおよび5台の実機ロボットを用いた実験により、提案手法の有効性と収束性を検証した。
keywords_ja: フォーメーション制御

2611.07091.title: Curvature by Design: A Support Structure for Continuum Robots
2611.07091.abstract: Constant- and piecewise-constant-curvature models are widely used to simplify the kinematics of continuum robots, although the assumed curvature profiles are not necessarily inherent mechanical properties of the robot and may therefore be violated during operation. Rather than assuming a prescribed curvature profile in the kinematic model and estimating deviations from it, this paper presents a multi-segment scissor-based support structure that mechanically constrains a continuum robot to exhibit prescribed constant or spatially varying curvature profiles. The design uses Taylor approximations to enable an overconstrained multi-joint linkage to predictably distribute global bending among the small-angle movements of multiple flexures. The geometric coupling is realized using compliant flexure joints, enabling the support structure to be manufactured as a single piece. The structure is integrated with a tendon-actuated continuum robot with a flexible backbone. Experiments show that the structure makes the robot resistant to deformations other than the prescribed curvature, significantly enhancing shape precision compared to classical flexible-backbone designs. This constrains the robot from making S-shapes when external loads are applied in the opposite direction of the bending. By mechanically constraining the admissible deformation, the proposed structure reduces the number of independent shape variables that must be estimated.

llm.title_ja: デザインによる曲率：連続体ロボットのための支持構造
llm.tldr_ja: 連続体ロボットの運動学を機械的に制約し、所定の定常または空間的に変化する曲率プロファイルを示させる、マルチセグメントのシザーズ型支持構造を提案した。
llm.problem: 連続体ロボットのモデルで仮定される一定または区分的定常曲率のプロファイルは必ずしも本質的な機械的特性ではなく、動作中に破られる可能性があること。
llm.method: テーラー近似を用いて、過剰拘束された多関節リンケージが複数のフレクジャの小角度運動に大域的曲げを予測可能に分散させるマルチセグメント支持構造を設計する。
llm.result: 実験により、所定の曲率以外の変形に抵抗し、外部負荷が加わった際にも形状精度を大幅に向上させ、推定すべき独立した形状変数を削減できることを示した。

2611.06918.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
2611.06918.abstract: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. This raises a fundamental question: should action policies inherit a fixed visual endpoint, or directly access evolving visual computation? We introduce NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutional layers and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, allowing a flow-matching action expert to draw from instruction-conditioned visual representations at different depths. This simple change reveals a consistent pattern. Native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts under controlled comparisons; full fine-tuning reduces but does not erase the gap, and additional scale alone cannot recover it. More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control. Together, these results suggest that embodied control benefits from access to visual representations across the computational hierarchy, rather than a fixed encoder output.
2611.06918.hf_summary_en: NEO-VLA eliminates fixed visual encoders to let action policies access evolving visual representations across network depths, improving manipulation robustness.
2611.06918.tldr_en: NEO-VLA is introduced, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework that achieves stronger and more robust control and suggests that embodied control benefits from access to visual representations across the computational hierarchy, rather than a fixed encoder output.

llm.title_ja: ピクセルから行動へ - ネイティブなビジョン・言語・行動方策に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚エンコーダを排除し、パッチ畳み込み層によってトークン化された画像がバックボーン全体を通じて言語と共同で進化する、構造的にエンコーダフリーなVLAフレームワーク「NEO-VLA」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のVLAモデルは視覚情報が視覚エンコーダによって事前に圧縮されるため、マニピュレーションに不可欠な局所幾何学や境界、深度などの微妙な信号が失われること。
llm.method: 軽量なパッチ畳み込み層で画像をトークン化し、フローマッチング行動エキスパートが異なる深度の命令条件付き視覚表現から直接引き出せるようにする構造を採用する。
llm.result: 多様なマニピュレーション設定や分布シフトにおいて、エンコーダベースの従来の手法を上回る強力かつロバストな制御を実現した。

2611.06913.title: cuRoboV2-Fast: Fast Torque-Limited Collision-Free Motion Planning
2611.06913.abstract: We present cuRoboV2-Fast, a GPU-accelerated planner that reduces both planning latency and execution time for collision-free, payload-aware, torque-limited motions. B-spline trajectory optimization reduces the required iterations, while accelerated robot computations and differentiable inverse dynamics reduce refinement cost and accommodate changing payloads. TimeOpt optimizes traversal speed along the fixed path under sampled velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque constraints, exploiting local spline support to solve banded Newton systems efficiently on the GPU. With a 3,kg payload, cuRoboV2-Fast achieves 4.4 ms mean planning time on RTX 5090, 14.7x faster than cuRoboV2. Our method on Jetson AGX Orin plans faster than cuRoboV1 + TOPPRA on RTX 5090. A stereo-camera-based deployment on YAM achieves 5.93 s mean completed pick-and-drop cycles, 34.6% shorter than cuRoboV2. Code (Apache 2.0): www.github.com/NVlabs/curobo , Project Page: www.research.nvidia.com/labs/lpr/curobov2-fast .
2611.06913.tldr_en: cRoboV2-Fast is presented, a GPU-accelerated planner that reduces both planning latency and execution time for collision-free, payload-aware, torque-limited motions, and TimeOpt optimizes traversal speed along the fixed path under sampled velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque constraints.

llm.title_ja: cuRoboV2-Fast：高速なトルク制限付き衝突回避モーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: Bスプライン軌道最適化やGPU上での効率的なバンドニュートン系求解、TimeOptによる速度最適化により、計画レイテンシと実行時間を大幅に削減したGPU加速プランナー「cuRoboV2-Fast」を提案した。
llm.problem: 衝突回避、ペイロード考慮、トルク制限を満たしながら、リアルタイムで高速にロボットのモーションプランニングを行うこと。
llm.method: Bスプライン軌道最適化による反復回数の削減、微分可能逆動力学によるペイロード変更への対応、およびGPU上でのTimeOptによる速度・加速度・トルク制約下の最適化を統合する。
llm.result: RTX 5090上で3kgのペイロードに対し4.4msの平均計画時間を達成し、cuRoboV2と比較して14.7倍高速化するとともに、実機のピック＆ドロップサイクルを大幅に短縮した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.06911.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
2611.06911.abstract: Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories (SDCLs) are moving chemical experimentation toward embodied automation, where machines must perceive laboratory scenes, reason about experimental states, and act under physical, procedural, and safety constraints. Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly considered as embodied brains for such systems, existing laboratory benchmarks mainly focus on safety, anomaly detection, or general scientific understanding, leaving their execution-oriented embodied capabilities underexplored. To fill this gap, we introduce BEAKER, a Benchmark for evaluating Embodied Actionability, Knowledge, Experimentation, and Reasoning in SDCLs. BEAKER contains 1,000 expert-curated question-answer samples across 11 image and video task types, covering key judgments required for chemical laboratory execution, including affordance grounding, trajectory planning, equipment, state, and safety recognition, apparatus setup, operation and step reasoning, and temporal procedure reasoning. All questions and annotations are manually created and reviewed by chemistry and embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) experts, without AI-assisted generation or annotation. We evaluate 28 general-purpose, science-oriented, chemistry-specialized, and embodied MLLMs in an offline, single-turn setting. Results show that current models can follow coarse experimental procedures in videos, but still struggle to ground actions into operable regions and feasible trajectories, to recognize fine-grained laboratory apparatus, states, and safety norms, and to order steps in mid-length procedures. BEAKER thus reveals a clear gap between coarse procedural understanding and the precise, action-grounded perception required for laboratory execution, providing a diagnostic benchmark for future MLLMs in SDCLs.
2611.06911.comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026 (Track on Evaluations and Datasets, Spotlight)
2611.06911.tldr_en: BEAKER reveals a clear gap between coarse procedural understanding and the precise, action-grounded perception required for laboratory execution, providing a diagnostic benchmark for future MLLMs in SDCLs.

llm.title_ja: BEAKER：自動化学実験室における身体化された頭脳のための専門家キュレーション型ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 化学実験室の自動化（SDCL）におけるマルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）の実行指向の身体化能力を評価するため、専門家がキュレーションした1,000のQ&Aサンプルからなるベンチマーク「BEAKER」を構築した。
llm.problem: 従来の実験室向けベンチマークは安全性や異常検知、一般的な科学的理解に主眼が置かれており、実行指向の身体化された能力が十分に探求されていないこと。
llm.method: アフォーダンスの接地、軌道計画、器具・状態・安全性の認識、装置のセットアップ、手順推論など11のタスクタイプにわたる1,000の質問応答サンプルを専門家が手動で作成・レビューする。
llm.result: 28の多様なMLLMを評価した結果、大まかな手順の理解と、実験実行に必要な精密で行動に根ざした知覚との間に明確なギャップが存在することを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2611.06908.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
2611.06908.abstract: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which require at least an hour of human time to produce an hour of data. We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes. The corpus scales with compute rather than human labor. HALO acquires a repertoire of physical skills, including sitting on chairs, navigating to named objects, stepping sideways through half-open doors, crouching and crawling beneath tables, and pushing boxes. It orchestrates these skills to solve composite, long-horizon tasks. Without ever seeing a real home during training, HALO transfers zero-shot to the physical world, achieving a 91% success rate across 360 trials in six unmapped real-world environments. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-halo/ for code and videos.
2611.06908.tldr_en: HALO is presented, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes and orchestrates these skills to solve composite, long-horizon tasks.

llm.title_ja: シミュレーションからの知覚的ヒューマノイドモーション
llm.tldr_ja: 1,000のプロシージャル生成された家屋環境で視覚・言語・モーションデータを合成するパイプラインにより、人間の手作業なしで多様な物理的スキルと長期タスクを学習し実世界へゼロショット移行するヒューマノイド自律システム「HALO」を提案した。
llm.problem: ピクセルや自由形式の言語を低レベルの関節指令にマッピングするための大規模なペア教師データの不足（データボトルネック）。
llm.method: 1,000以上の手続き型生成ホーム環境でビジョン・言語・モーションデータを大規模に合成し、椅子への座り、物体への移動、障害物の回避・くぐり抜けなどの物理的スキルを学習させる。
llm.result: 訓練時に実世界の家屋を一度も見ていないにもかかわらず、マッピングされていない6つの実世界の環境における360回の試行で91%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
シミュレーション合成

2611.06905.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
2611.06905.abstract: The introduction of generalist robot policies has enabled a single, large model to learn to perform a variety of tasks from a vast pre-training corpus. While these models often exhibit powerful zero-shot generalization capabilities, they typically require an adaptation phase to achieve sufficient performance in deployment. Iterated self-improvement via reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated promise in enabling this adaptation, yet such approaches have been largely explored in single-task settings - where the goal is to simply improve on a narrow deployment task - which lies in stark contrast to the multi-task capabilities of the base policy. In this work we ask whether generalist robot policies are capable of multi-task, generalist improvement in deployment - targeting many diverse tasks simultaneously - and what algorithmic recipe enables this. To answer this question, we first develop a set of structured evaluations to test generalist improvement capabilities, and systematically evaluate algorithmic and practical design choices regarding value estimation, policy extraction and resource allocation. We show that not only can generalist policies be improved online across diverse tasks, but that the right recipe can enable generalization and increase performance on tasks not considered during online training. We characterize when this generalization occurs and show that both the training task distribution and the use of value-based RL are critical. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first evidence for online generalist improvement for robot foundation models.
2611.06905.tldr_en: It is shown that not only can generalist policies be improved online across diverse tasks, but that the right recipe can enable generalization and increase performance on tasks not considered during online training.

llm.title_ja: 強化学習による汎用ロボット方策の改善のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 多様なタスクを同時にターゲットとするマルチタスクかつ汎用的なオンライン改善が汎用ロボット方策において可能であることを示し、値ベース強化学習と訓練タスク分布の重要性を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 汎用ロボット方策は強力なゼロショット汎化能力を持つ一方で、デプロイ時に十分な性能を発揮するために適応フェーズが必要であり、これまでの自己改善は単一タスクに限定されていたこと。
llm.method: 値推定、方策抽出、リソース配分のアルゴリズム的・実用的な設計選択を体系的に評価し、オンラインでのマルチタスク汎用改善の条件を検証する。
llm.result: 適切なレシピを用いることで、多様なタスクにわたるオンラインでの汎用方策の改善が可能となり、オンライン訓練中に考慮していなかったタスクの性能や汎化性も向上することを示した。

2611.06901.title: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models
2611.06901.abstract: JEPA-style world models learn action-conditioned latent dynamics without reconstructing observations, but distributional regularization alone does not ensure that their representations preserve information needed for control. We identify static collapse, a failure mode in which the encoder preserves episode-specific static content while suppressing manipulation-relevant state changes. Because static content is temporally predictable yet diverse across episodes, this failure can persist despite regularizers such as SIGReg. A controlled study on OGBench-Cube shows that introducing randomized backgrounds substantially degrades planning performance while leaving the underlying manipulation task unchanged. To address this problem, we propose motion-guided contrastive regularization. Our approach compares predicted latent transitions with transitions to candidate observations from the same episode, reducing the usefulness of static background identity for distinguishing action outcomes. Optical-flow similarities provide soft contrastive targets, allowing candidates with similar motion to receive similar supervision. Combined with latent prediction and SIGReg, our objective encourages representations to preserve within-episode state distinctions and similarities between related transitions. Our method improves planning success over LeWorldModel (LeWM) from 52% to 78% on OGBench-Cube with randomized backgrounds and from 14% to 54% on LIBERO-Object, while maintaining comparable performance on four other visual-control benchmarks.
2611.06901.tldr_en: This work identifies static collapse, a failure mode in which the encoder preserves episode-specific static content while suppressing manipulation-relevant state changes, and proposes motion-guided contrastive regularization, a approach that improves planning success over LeWorldModel and from 14% to 54% on LIBERO-Object, while maintaining comparable performance on four other visual-control benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: 潜在世界モデルのためのモーション誘導型対照正則化
llm.tldr_ja: エンコーダがマニピュレーションに関連する状態変化を抑制してしまう「静的崩壊」という失敗モードを特定し、オプティカルフローの類似性を活用してマニピュレーション性能を向上させるモーション誘導型対照正則化手法を提案した。
llm.problem: JEPAスタイルの世界モデルにおいて、分布正則化だけではエンコーダの表現が制御に必要な情報を保持することを保証できず、静的崩壊を引き起こすこと。
llm.method: 予測された潜在遷移を同一エピソード内の候補観測からの遷移と比較し、オプティカルフローの類似性をソフトな対照ターゲットとして利用して状態変化の表現を促す。
llm.result: ランダム化された背景を持つOGBench-CubeやLIBERO-Objectにおいて、LeWorldModel等と比較して計画成功率を大幅に向上させた（OGBench-Cubeで52%から78%へ向上）。

2611.06899.title: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues
2611.06899.abstract: Knowing that a pedestrian is occluded is useful to a robot even when the detector cannot recover the hidden pixels, but occlusion estimators are normally trained on occlusion annotations that deployment settings rarely have. We show that occlusion can be read off two distance estimates a camera-only pipeline already computes. Apparent height is largely unchanged by occlusion, because the detected box still spans the whole person; monocular metric depth is pulled toward the occluder, because the nearest surface inside the box is what a depth map reports. Only their ordering matters, so no focal length, stature, or depth scale is needed, provided the depth model's error is close to a pure gain, a condition that can be checked without labels. The score detects heavy occlusion on KITTI with AUC 0.909 (0.888 over all annotated pedestrians, including those the detector misses), requires no training and no occlusion labels, and is not a proxy for range: within fixed distance bands it holds AUC 0.894-0.925 while true distance alone sits near chance. On synthetic CARLA scenes with measured visibility it reaches 0.819, against 0.644 for distance alone. We arrived here after measuring three standard architectural responses to occlusion, depth fusion, occlusion-simulating augmentation, and attention, none of which improved detection outside its training distribution in the configurations we tested, and after finding that a detector trained on German roads loses half its accuracy on self-annotated street scenes in Lagos, Nigeria. Signals that need no local annotation are worth more in settings that benchmarks do not represent.
2611.06899.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 GlobalSouthAI Workshop
2611.06899.tldr_en: It is shown that occlusion can be read off two distance estimates a camera-only pipeline already computes, and signals that need no local annotation are worth more in settings that benchmarks do not represent.

llm.title_ja: 追加学習不要のオクルージョン検出：2つの単眼距離キューの不一致からのオクルージョン検出
llm.tldr_ja: カメラ単体のパイプラインですでに計算されている2つの距離推定値（外観上の高さと単眼メトリック深度）の不一致から、追加の学習やオクルージョン注釈なしで歩行者のオクルージョンを高精度に検出できる手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 歩行者が隠れている（オクルージョンされている）ことを検出することは有用だが、オクルージョン推定器の訓練にはデプロイ環境では稀なオクルージョン注釈が必要であること。
llm.method: 検出されたバックスパンに基づく外観上の高さと、オクルージョンにより手前の表面に引っ張られる単眼メトリック深度の順序の不一致を利用してスコアを算出する。
llm.result: KITTIデータセットにおいてAUC 0.909を達成し、訓練やオクルージョン注釈を一切必要とせずに重度のオクルージョンを効果的に検出できることを示した。

2611.06881.title: VABAR: A Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics
2611.06881.abstract: For robots to operate reliably in commercial and industrial applications, they must persistently perform specific tasks with known variations in object shape and pose. We call this Variational Automation (VA) to differentiate these settings from fixed automation. Inspired by recent papers on Agentic Robotics, where pretrained LLM and VLM coding agents combine interpretable robot programming with the open-world adaptability of model free policies, we propose a general set of agentic robotics benchmark design criteria that includes accessibility, repeatability, diversity, relevance to agentic robotics and practical applications, physical realizability, resistance to benchmark saturation, and computational efficiency. We instantiate these principles in six manipulation task classes spanning industrial, medical, and infrastructure applications: tool sorting, tool hanging, gear meshing, syringe packing, cable insertion, and cable routing. We introduce the Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics (VABAR), an open, easily replicable, simulation-based manipulation benchmark to systematically evaluating agentic robotics systems. Built fully on open-source tools, VABAR features detailed implementations using the Newton physics engine, standardized task variations, difficulty tiers, success metrics, and a library of 33 generalizable skills with human-authored programmatic reference solutions. We provide initial baseline evaluations using an open agentic manipulation harness, Graph-as-Policy (GaP), and Isaac Lab Arena.
2611.06881.tldr_en: A general set of agentic robotics benchmark design criteria that includes accessibility, repeatability, diversity, relevance to agentic robotics and practical applications, physical realizability, resistance to benchmark saturation, and computational efficiency is proposed.

llm.title_ja: VABAR：エージェント型ロボティクスのための変動自動化ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: エージェント型ロボティクスシステムの体系的な評価のため、アクセシビリティや多様性などの基準を満たすオープンなシミュレーションベースのマニピュレーションベンチマークVABARを提案する。
llm.problem: 変動自動化におけるロボットの信頼性評価のための標準的なベンチマークが不足している。
llm.method: 産業・医療・インフラを網羅する6つのマニピュレーションタスクと33のスキルライブラリからなるシミュレーションベンチマークを構築する。
llm.result: Isaac Lab Arenaを用いたベースライン評価を実装し、エージェント型マニピュレーションの体系的評価を可能にした。
keywords_ja: エージェント型ロボティクス

2611.06863.title: Rethinking Self-Repair in Code-as-Policy Agents: What Drives Retry Success?
2611.06863.abstract: Code-as-policy agents often use execution feedback to retry failed programs. Additional sampling and task guidance can also improve success, leaving the contribution of failure-specific feedback unclear. We study this question in simulated robot manipulation. A fixed lookup selects feedback templates using failure labels and the API variant. A frozen code model generates a fresh program after each scene reset. On the same 252 initial failures, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B recovers 85.3% within five retries, compared with 68.3% for resampling with the same retry cap. The advantage persists under fixed total-token budgets. Feedback from other episodes and fixed task guidance yield similar recovery point estimates, with no detected benefit from matching the coarse failure label. In a separate study, a fixed guided prompt used from the first attempt achieves an observed overall success rate similar to that of template-based feedback. Template-based feedback also lowers recovery on a nut-insertion task requiring a rim grasp, consistent with an incompatible center-grasp instruction. Evaluations of robot self-repair should include resampling, mismatched feedback, and concise, task-compatible static guidance as baselines.
2611.06863.comment: Accepted to the CoRL 2026 Learn@Deploy workshop
2611.06863.tldr_en: Evaluations of robot self-repair should include resampling, mismatched feedback, and concise, task-compatible static guidance as baselines, and a fixed guided prompt used from the first attempt achieves an observed overall success rate similar to that of template-based feedback.

2611.06817.title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
2611.06817.abstract: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.
2611.06817.tldr_en: Open-HumanScale is introduced, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanScale-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language.

llm.title_ja: Open-HumanWAM：身体性基盤モデルのための人間とロボットの経験スケーリングに向けたオープンなレシピ
llm.tldr_ja: 5万時間の視点映像を用いた初の完全オープンな事前学習レシピOpen-HumanWAMを開発し、シミュレーションおよび実機で優れた汎化性能とゼロショット適応を示した。
llm.problem: 膨大な生データから汎用的なロボットポリシーへのスケーリングには厳格なデータキュレーションと学習レシピが必要である。
llm.method: 5万時間の視点動画コーパスを用いた世界・行動モデルの事前学習、および人間・ロボットの結合事前学習を行う。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0でClean2Clean 92.70%を達成し、実機においても事前のパラメータ更新なしでの動的適応を実現した。

2611.06802.title: ConDR: Conservative Reachability through Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Subsolutions
2611.06802.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) Reachability identifies the unsafe states of a dynamical system from which it can be forced into failure under worst-case disturbance. However, classical grid-based solvers scale exponentially with state dimension. DeepReach improves scalability by replacing the grid with a neural value function trained on the HJ-Isaacs (HJI) variational inequality (VI), but penalizes both sides of the residual equally. This allows the learned value to lie above the true one and unsafe states to be misclassified as safe. We propose Conservative DeepReach (ConDR) which aims to learn a subsolution of the HJI VI such that the learned unsafe set contains the true one. ConDR enforces the obstacle branch and terminal condition by construction, pushes the HJI residual to a safety margin $ε$ below zero with a one-sided loss, and prevents the degenerate solution of classifying everything as unsafe. We prove that the exact solution of the margin-shifted VI that ConDR trains toward is a subsolution of the original VI so its unsafe set contains the true one and its value lies within $ετ$ of the true value function. We compare against DeepReach and MADR in the established systems of Air3D, Air6D, a 9D multi-vehicle system, and a 13D quadrotor. ConDR reports the lowest rate of unsafe state misclassified and the lowest closed-loop collision rates with at most a small increase in intervention. On Air3D and Air6D, ConDR tolerates model mismatch that scales with $ε$. At matched false-negative rates, ConDR's unsafe sets are smaller than the baselines showing the safety is not obtained by trivial over-approximation.
2611.06802.tldr_en: It is proved that the exact solution of the margin-shifted VI that ConDR trains toward is a subsolution of the original VI so its unsafe set contains the true one and its value lies within $\epsilon\tau$ of the true value function.

llm.title_ja: ConDR：ニューラルハミルトン・ヤコビ部分解による保守的到達可能解析
llm.tldr_ja: ニューラルネットワークを用いてハミルトン・ヤコビ変分不等式の保守的な部分解を学習し、安全でない状態の誤分類や衝突率を削減するConDRを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のグリッドベースのハミルトン・ヤコビ到達可能解析は次元数に対して指数関数的にスケーリングし、学習された値の誤差により危険状態が安全と誤認される。
llm.method: 障害物条件を組み込み、片側損失を用いてHJI残差を安全マージン以下に押し下げるConDRを学習する。
llm.result: Air3D、Air6D、9Dマルチビークル、13Dクアドロータルのシステムにおいて、最も低い安全状態の誤分類率と閉ループ衝突率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ハミルトン・ヤコビ方程式
ニューラルネットワーク

2611.06768.title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
2611.06768.abstract: Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. In this work, we study embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement. Our empirical study places physical manipulation at the center of the improvement process, examining how agents collaborate, what kinds of execution feedback support effective code refinement, and how task specifications and previously acquired skills influence robustness and task transfer. We further investigate the efficiency and capability of the resulting programs when deployed without involving an online agent for decision-making. Across eight real-world tasks, PyRUA-REAL achieves an average success rate of 91.1%. In complementary evaluation on 42 tasks from the RoboDojo benchmark, it achieves an average success rate of 84.4%. This study provides empirical guidance for turning physical exploration into reusable robot skills that support continued improvement and robust, efficient deployment.
2611.06768.tldr_en: This work studies embodied recursive self-improvement through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement.
2611.06768.hf_summary_en: PyRUA-REAL enables coding agents to convert physical robot exploration into persistent executable skills, achieving high success rates across real-world and benchmark tasks through recursive self-improvement.

llm.title_ja: PyRUA-REAL：現実世界におけるRSIを通じたロボットの探索と適応学習
llm.tldr_ja: コーディングエージェントが実世界での探索とコード洗練を通じてインタラクション経験を永続的な記憶と再利用可能なスキルとして保持するフレームワークPyRUA-REALを提案する。
llm.problem: 空間推論と実行可能なロボット行動を結びつけるコーディングエージェントにおいて、物理的インタラクションから持続的な能力向上を得る方法が課題である。
llm.method: 探索、コード洗練、デプロイを統合した身体的再帰的自己改善（RSI）フレームワークを実装し、実世界のマニピュレーションタスクで評価する。
llm.result: 8つの実世界タスクで平均91.1%、RoboDojoベンチマークの42タスクで平均84.4%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: コーディングエージェント

2611.06724.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
2611.06724.abstract: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages. We organize the literature into five interdependent layers: hardware; data collection and curation; cross-embodiment transfer; learning and foundation models; and evaluation and applications. Human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing provide two cross-cutting perspectives. A system-level architecture, comparative tables and five case analyses connect design choices across these layers. We distinguish within-study experimental comparisons from heterogeneous corpus statistics, vendor specifications and company-reported results. Three conclusions emerge. First, the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment, not recording volume alone. Second, shared action representations and foundation policies do not remove embodiment-specific constraints on force, latency and contact. Third, task completion is insufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness. Evidence remains limited for zero-shot transfer of contact-rich skills between morphologically different hands, long-duration reliability, and cross-sensor tactile generalization. We identify eleven open problems and propose reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable. The review is a structured narrative synthesis rather than a pooled performance ranking or an exhaustive systematic review.
2611.06724.comment: 45 pages, 8 figures, 21 tables. Structured narrative review of hardware, data, cross-embodiment transfer, foundation models, tactile sensing, and evaluation for dexterous robotic hands
2611.06724.tldr_en: This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages and identifies eleven open problems and proposed reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable.

llm.title_ja: 基盤モデル時代の器用なロボットハンド：ハードウェア、データ、クロスエンボディメント転移、学習、評価のフルスタックサーベイ
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模な人間データと基盤モデルに結び付けられた器用なロボットハンドに関する、2024年1月から2026年11月までの文献を網羅的にサーベイする。
llm.problem: 器用なロボットハンドのハードウェア、表現学習、評価に関する進展が個別に評価されており、全体像の整理が必要である。
llm.method: ハードウェア、データ収集、クロスエンボディメント転移、基盤モデルによる学習、評価・応用の5つの層に分類して文献を構造的に統合する。
llm.result: 人間データの価値、共有行動表現の限界、物理的正確性の評価に関する3つの結論を導き、11のオープンな課題を特定した。
llm.limitation: 接触豊富なスキルのゼロショット転移、長期信頼性、クロスセンサ触覚一般化の証拠は依然として限られている。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント転移

2611.06710.title: Where Is VLA Inference Time Spent? Bottlenecks and Optimization Interactions Across GPUs
2611.06710.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models map camera observations and language instructions to robot actions. However, their large backbones and repeated action generation can make inference take longer than the robot's real-time requirements for its next action. To reduce the load of VLA computations, researchers have proposed multiple optimization approaches, including quantization and pruning. These optimizations can be combined with other general optimizations such as better kernel compilation or using CUDA graphs instead of the eager mode. However, most of these optimization results are usually reported on a single GPU type, typically for a few VLA models, with no analysis of what the real bottlenecks are for a model on a particular hardware or how these optimizations would generalize beyond the reported results. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive measurement study of seven families of inference optimization methods, from CUDA graphs and compilation to token pruning and quantization, on seven state-of-the-art VLAs evaluated on four GPU families ranging from a datacenter H100 to an embedded Jetson Thor. We analyse how CPU launch overhead, memory bandwidth, and kernel efficiency jointly shape optimization gains, and how applying one method changes the benefit of another. From this analysis, we derive VLA-Triage, guidelines for stacking optimizations under latency budgets. The guidelines identify which stages can provide the required savings and which combinations need testing in the deployed execution mode.
2611.06710.tldr_en: From this analysis, VLA-Triage, guidelines for stacking optimizations under latency budgets are derived, which identify which stages can provide the required savings and which combinations need testing in the deployed execution mode.

llm.title_ja: VLA推論時間はどこで消費されているのか？：GPU間におけるボトルネックと最適化の相互作用
llm.tldr_ja: 7種類の最先端VLAモデルと4種類のGPUファミリーを用いて推論最適化手法の網羅的な測定を行い、レイテンシ予算内で最適化を組み合わせるためのガイドラインを導出した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルの大規模バックボーンと反復的な行動生成により、リアルタイム要件を満たすには推論時間が長すぎるが、最適化手法の一般化やボトルネックの分析が不足している。
llm.method: CUDAグラフやコンパイルからトークンプルーニング、量子化までの7種類の最適化手法を多様なGPU上で包括的に評価し分析する。
llm.result: CPU起動オーバーヘッド、メモリ帯域幅、カーネル効率が最適化の利得に与える影響を明らかにし、VLA-Triageガイドラインを提案した。

2611.06702.title: When to Ask for Help: Uncertainty-Triggered Aerial Refinement for Off-Road Navigation
2611.06702.abstract: Heterogeneous air-ground teams can use aerial sensing to address the limited range and viewpoint of ground-vehicle sensors, but deciding when the UGV needs assistance and what information the UAV should collect remains a challenge. This paper presents a planner-conditioned air-ground assistance method that evaluates how uncertain map information affects the UGV's current MPPI rollouts. When navigation remains degraded, we score the same rollouts under resolved map hypotheses, select the map layer with the largest useful improvement, request the corresponding aerial measurement, fuse the returned information, and replan. Unlike approaches driven by fixed support roles, task structure, or uncertainty alone, our method conditions assistance on whether resolving uncertainty improves predicted ground navigation. Across 180 simulation trials on three off-road routes, the method achieves 98.9% goal attainment while reducing mean UAV flight time by 87.7% relative to continuous greedy aerial mapping. Aggregated across the routes, each second of estimated UAV flight time saves 2.94 s of UGV navigation time. Field experiments spanning approximately 2 km of UGV operation demonstrate uncertainty resolution and successful navigation recovery.
2611.06702.tldr_en: This paper presents a planner-conditioned air-ground assistance method that evaluates how uncertain map information affects the UGV's current MPPI rollouts and conditions assistance on whether resolving uncertainty improves predicted ground navigation.

llm.title_ja: 助けを求めるタイミング：オフロードナビゲーションのための不確実性トリガー型空中リファインメント
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実なマップ情報の解決が地上車両のナビゲーションを改善するかどうかに基づいて空中支援を条件付ける、プランナー条件付き空中地上協調手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 不均一な空地チームにおいて、地上車両（UGV）がいつ支援を必要とし、無人航空機（UAV）がどのような情報を収集すべきかの判断が課題である。
llm.method: 不確実なマップ情報がUGVのMPPIロールアウトに与えどの影響を評価し、不確実性解決が予測ナビゲーションを改善する場合にのみ空中計測を要求してリプランする。
llm.result: 180回のシミュレーション試行で98.9%の目標到達率を達成し、連続的な欲張り型空中マッピングと比較してUAVの飛行時間を87.7%削減した。

2611.06689.title: Cognitive and Behavioural Effects of Haptic Feedback for ROV Teleoperation in Hazardous Environments
2611.06689.abstract: Teleoperating a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) in complex underwater environments presents unique challenges. Dynamic, three dimensional obstacles and unseen water currents pose real risks to expensive robotic hardware in environments in which recovery can be next to impossible. This paper explores the cognitive effects of haptic feedback to improve vehicle safety in such environments. An in-water study is analysed with a ROV exposed to controlled cross-currents, with environmental information presented via a soft and vibrating haptic touchpad. Results demonstrate that while encountering an unseen cross-current significantly increases an operator's physical and temporal demand, the introduction of haptic feedback mitigates these factors and improves self-assessed performance. Interestingly, the haptic condition also produced the highest levels of mental demand and operator frustration. Despite this increased mental workload, operators drove the ROV significantly faster when receiving haptic cues compared to the current-only condition, indicating a higher level of user confidence. Ultimately, these findings suggest that while haptic feedback may initially require more cognitive processing to interpret unseen hazards, it successfully enhances operator awareness and promotes more confident navigation in hazardous environments.

llm.title_ja: 危険環境におけるROV遠隔操作のための触覚フィードバックの認知的および行動的効果
llm.tldr_ja: 水中での遠隔操作ロボット（ROV）において、ソフトで振動する触覚パッドを用いた環境情報の提示がオペレータの認知負荷や行動に与える影響を水中実験で分析した。
llm.problem: 水中環境でのROV遠隔操作では、動的な障害物や見えない水流がハードウェアに深刻なリスクをもたらす。
llm.method: 制御された横風にさらされるROVを用いた水中実験を通じて、触覚フィードバックがオペレータの認知的・身体的負荷とパフォーマンスに与える影響を評価する。
llm.result: 触覚フィードバックにより物理的・時間的要求が緩和され自己評価パフォーマンスが向上する一方、精神的負荷やフラストレーションも増加し、自信の向上により操作速度が有意に向上した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.06673.title: Which Physical Tactile Cues Matter for Contact-Rich Imitation Learning? A Controlled Real-Robot Study
2611.06673.abstract: Vision-based tactile sensors capture multiple aspects of physical interaction within a single image stream, including contact appearance, geometry, indentation depth, and tangential deformation. However, existing visuo-tactile policies often directly process tactile observations as images, making it difficult to determine which physical cues contribute to policy learning. This paper presents a controlled real-robot study that compares physically interpretable tactile signals using the LeRobot platform, enhanced with our visuo-tactile perception system. From the same tactile stream, we derive tactile RGB images, normal/depth maps, and marker-flow fields, representing contact appearance, geometry, and tangential deformation, respectively. Using identical task demonstrations and the same policy backbone, we evaluate the individual and combined contributions of these tactile cues. We further compare tactile encoders and visuo-tactile fusion strategies. Evaluation across 720 real-robot trials yields four key findings: (1) tactile perception substantially improves the overall success rate from 57.8% to 78.9%, although its contribution varies across task stages; (2) marker flow is the most effective individual cue, achieving a success rate of 74.4% and playing a particularly important role in regulating established contact; (3) cue-factorized encoding consistently improves performance, highlighting that different physical cues require tailored processing techniques; and (4) although the effectiveness of tactile fusion is task-dependent, cross-attention offers a lightweight solution with performance comparable to that of pretrained tactile encoders.
2611.06673.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to IEEE ROBIO 2026
2611.06673.tldr_en: A controlled real-robot study that compares physically interpretable tactile signals using the LeRobot platform, enhanced with the authors' visuo-tactile perception system, and finds cross-attention offers a lightweight solution with performance comparable to that of pretrained tactile encoders.

llm.title_ja: 接触リッチな模倣学習において重要な物理的触覚手がかりとは何か：制御された実機ロボット研究
llm.tldr_ja: LeRobotプラットフォームを用いた制御された実機実験により、接触外観、幾何学、接線変形などの触覚手がかりの模倣学習への貢献度を比較評価した。
llm.problem: 既存の視覚・触覚ポリシーは触覚観察を直接画像として処理するため、どの物理的手がかりがポリシー学習に寄与しているかの判断が困難である。
llm.method: 同一のタスクデモとポリシーバックボーンを用い、触覚RGB画像、法線/深度マップ、マーカー流れ場を個別にまたは組み合わせて評価する。
llm.result: 触覚知覚により全体的な成功率が57.8%から78.9%に向上し、マーカー流れが確立された接触の調整に最も効果的な個別手がかりであることを示した。

2611.06654.title: Compounding Physical RSI: Turning Execution Failure into Inherited Capability
2611.06654.abstract: Generalist robot policies are trained on static offline datasets, yet physical manipulation unfolds sequentially across stages. Because a weakness in a downstream stage remains unobservable until the policy passes earlier ones, each resolved bottleneck exposes the next hidden failure mode. This staged structure calls for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), in which a policy iteratively executes, diagnoses failures, and updates itself. Moreover, because task completion behaves like a product of stage-level pass rates, recursive gains can multiply across generations. In physical environments, three bottlenecks obstruct compounding: terminal execution feedback rarely localizes the stage that caused a failure, failed trajectories do not supply the corrective action, and updating shared parameters can degrade previously mastered skills. We propose Compounding Physical RSI, a self-evolving policy framework that turns execution failures into heritable capability. First, automated capability-gap assessment traces failed rollouts to the task stage where progression breaks down and formulates a structured improvement objective. Second, conditioned on this objective, our remedy stage curates validated, stage-relevant experience and refines the policy via behavior-regularized offline reinforcement learning, without requiring costly online rollouts at each optimization step. Third, to safeguard existing skills, our retention stage constructs weight-space candidates between the inherited reference policy and the refined policy, evaluates them across the task suite, and promotes the best candidate as the reference state for the next generation. Evaluated across all 42 tasks of the RoboDojo-Sim benchmark, CSU-AI-07 ranks first on the leaderboard with a three-seed mean Overall Score of 26.15 and Success Rate of 20.70%, outperforming the next-best entry by 5.92 points and 5.82 percentage points.
2611.06654.tldr_en: Compounding Physical RSI, a self-evolving policy framework that turns execution failures into heritable capability, is proposed, a self-evolving policy framework that turns execution failures into heritable capability.

llm.title_ja: 物理的RSIの複合化：実行失敗を継承可能な能力へと変える
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシーの実行失敗をタスクステージごとに診断・修正し、既存スキルを保持しながら再帰的自己改善を行うフレームワーク「Compounding Physical RSI」を提案する。
llm.problem: 汎用ロボットポリシーは静的なオフラインデータで学習されるが、下流ステージの弱点は上流が成功するまで観測できず、物理環境では失敗の局所化やパラメータ劣化などのボトルネックがある。
llm.method: 自動能力ギャップ評価によるステージ診断、行動正則化オフライン強化学習による改善、および重み空間候補の評価・保持を行うセルフエボビングポリシーフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: RoboDojo-Simベンチマークの42タスク全てにおいて、CSU-AI-07が3シード平均の総合スコアでリーダーボード1位を獲得した。

2611.06653.title: Detecting Silent Action-Interface Mismatch with Calibrated Relational World Models
2611.06653.abstract: A robot action can satisfy shape and range constraints yet carry the wrong semantics: axes may be permuted, signs inverted, rotations rescaled, or gripper polarity reversed. We study learned state-action-effect relations as offline contracts for detecting these mismatches and ranking their likely fields. Clean held-out transitions calibrate alarms; a fixed inverse vocabulary supports closed-set localization. On ten LIBERO Spatial tasks comprising 432 source episodes, a capacity-controlled comparison at 2.5% empirical clean false-positive rate gives 46.1% recall for a ridge forward residual, 61.0% for a four-component joint Gaussian mixture, and 65.7% for the exact conditional of that same mixture. The joint score retains a 14.9 percentage-point advantage over ridge, while conditioning improves recall by a further 4.7 points. Joint scoring instead has higher localization: 95.8% versus 94.6%. These matched-rate comparisons are retrospective diagnostics, not deployment calibration guarantees. Earlier Object/Goal results broaden tasks within the LIBERO convention; DROID, all three HYDRA tasks, short temporal faults, small offsets, exact repair, and simulated mitigation fail their respective gates, while xArm contributes one task only. The evidence supports a bounded offline diagnostic and a detection-localization tradeoff, rather than joint-density superiority or cross-robot safety.
2611.06653.comment: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Modeling Uncertainty in Robotic World Models (UncertainWM). 20 pages, including 12 pages of supplementary material
2611.06653.tldr_en: The evidence supports a bounded offline diagnostic and a detection-localization tradeoff, rather than joint-density superiority or cross-robot safety, rather than joint-density superiority or cross-robot safety.

llm.title_ja: 較正された関係型世界モデルを用いたサイレント行動・インタフェースミスマッチの検出
llm.tldr_ja: 学習された状態・行動・効果の関係性をオフラインの契約として利用し、ロボットの軸の順序や符号の反転などのサイレントミスマッチを検出・局所化する手法を研究した。
llm.problem: ロボットの行動が形状や範囲の制約を満たしていても、軸の置換や符号の反転などの誤ったセマンティクスを持つ場合がある。
llm.method: クリーンなホールドアウト遷移を用いてアラームを較正し、厳密な条件付き混合ガウスモデルなどによるオフライン診断を行う。
llm.result: LIBERO Spatialタスクを用いた評価において、リッジ回帰残差やガウス混合モデルを比較し、結合スコアが優れた局所化性能（95.8%）を持つことを示した。
llm.limitation: クロスロボットの安全性やジョイント密度の優位性ではなく、限定的なオフライン診断と検出・局所化のトレードオフを支持する結果となった。

2611.06652.title: Dynamical State-Space Diffusion for Spatiotemporal Prediction
2611.06652.abstract: Diffusion models for temporal prediction typically corrupt each future frame with independent noise, leaving temporal dependence entirely to the denoiser. We propose Dynamical State-Space Diffusion (DSSD), which learns the temporal structure of the corruption process itself. DSSD builds a temporal kernel from the damped oscillatory modes of a stable diagonal state-space model, whose learned decay rates and frequencies let the corruption capture multiple timescales and oscillatory correlations, while the denoiser architecture remains unchanged. Running this model on a finite clip, however, requires the state before the first frame, which is unobserved; starting from a zero state leaves the early frames with less noise than the diffusion schedule prescribes. We avoid this by using the Cholesky factor of the model's stationary covariance as the temporal operator. We prove that this operator is causal, exactly invertible, keeps each frame's noise variance equal to that of standard diffusion, and reduces to the identity at the clean end of the process, and that it is exactly the Kalman innovations form of the state-space model. The denoiser is trained to predict the temporally correlated noise, and sampling removes and reapplies the temporal mixing at each step. On scientific-field and robot-video datasets, DSSD outperforms diffusion baselines that share its denoiser, and the evolution of its learned modes during training shows that the temporal operator adapts to each dataset.
2611.06652.tldr_en: DSSD builds a temporal kernel from the damped oscillatory modes of a stable diagonal state-space model, whose learned decay rates and frequencies let the corruption capture multiple timescales and oscillatory correlations, while the denoiser architecture remains unchanged.

llm.title_ja: 時空間予測のための動的状態空間拡散
llm.tldr_ja: 安定な対角状態空間モデルの減衰振動モードから時空間カーネルを構築し、拡散プロセスの破損プロセス自体の時間的構造を学習するDSSDを提案する。
llm.problem: 時系列予測のための拡散モデルは各未来フレームを独立したノイズで破損させるため、時間的依存性をデノイザーに完全に依存している。
llm.method: モデルの定常共分散のコレスキー因子を時間的演算子として使用し、因果的で正確に反転可能でありながら標準拡散と同じノイズ分散を維持するDSSDを構築する。
llm.result: 科学分野およびロボット動画データセットにおいて、デノイザーを共有する従来の拡散ベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2611.06649.title: SCRUB: Contact-Based Surface-Frame Estimation for Force-Motion Control with an Armless Quadruped
2611.06649.abstract: Wiping, sanding, and inspection robots press a sliding tool on a surface with controlled force. Controlling that force needs the surface normal, which is unknown on real-world, unmapped surfaces. Surface-normal estimators can help estimate the surface normal, but they either need a friction model or assume that the instantaneous tool velocity lies along the surface; however, walking violates this assumption. We propose SCRUB, a contact-based surface-frame estimator, which lets an armless quadruped slide a body-mounted tool along near-vertical surfaces in the absence of known, axis-aligned, or vision-predicted normals. SCRUB's predictive controller presses and slides the tool using a Kalman-filter estimate of the normal from two cues: 1) A force cue measures the estimate's tilt across the motion. If friction directly opposes the motion, the cue is zero exactly when that tilt is zero, for any friction coefficient. However, if the cue's sliding direction is wrong, friction appears as a false tilt. 2) A velocity cue measures tilt along the motion. Walking and pressing move the tool in and out. SCRUB therefore subtracts the commanded press rate from the tool velocity, averages the result over each gait cycle, and treats this mean as lying along the surface. On Unitree Go1 hardware at nominal speed and load, SCRUB completed every wall traverse and column orbit. No orbit completed with either cue removed, without gait averaging, or with a fixed normal.
